Verifier notes and special checks

Fifty-eight printed regions on two pages. The piece opens in 2/8 with five sharps, treble on the upper staff and bass on the lower staff, and a one-sixteenth pickup. The next fifty-six regions are ordinary full bars. No repeat, ending, meter change, key change, or clef change is printed; later systems only reprint the opening clefs and five sharps. The last region is one half-note chord on each staff, with a fermata, closed by a thin-and-thick final barline. Those printed strokes match the proposed frame.

  • System 1, P001: Is the opening region one sixteenth, after five sharps and the 2/8? Yes. The upper staff has one note with two flags and the lower staff has one rest with two hooks, and the next barline follows at once.
  • System 6, P058: Does the last region close on a final barline after a half-note chord? Yes. Each staff has one open notehead with a stem and no flags, a fermata stands over the upper chord, and the thin stroke at crop x 1626 stands just left of the thick stroke. No repeat dots are printed.
  • Systems 1 through 6: Is any repeat, ending, or later clef printed? No. Interior barlines are single thin strokes. Each later system reprints treble and bass with five sharps, and those reprints are not clef changes.
